contracts.grain: One row per CRM customer (customer_id), taken from one version of the customer's CDC records saved on or before @AsOfDate.

columns.name: initials
columns.description: SUBSTRING(x,0,2) in T-SQL returns only the first character, so this is the first letter of first_name plus the first letter of last_name, in upper case.

columns.name: email_shared_count
columns.description: Number of kept customer rows with the same email. 0 when email is NULL.

columns.name: age_at_join
columns.description: DATEDIFF(YEAR) from date_of_birth to customer_since. This counts calendar-year boundaries crossed, not completed years of age.

columns.name: region
columns.description: Sales region looked up from county. Counties not in the list, and NULL counties, get UNKNOWN.

columns.name: eircode_valid
columns.description: Checks length only: Y when the length is 7, or 8 with a space in position 4. T-SQL LEN ignores trailing spaces.

columns.name: is_standard_segment
columns.description: Y only when segment_code = 'STD'. segment_code is CHAR(4), so it is padded to 'STD '; T-SQL ignores trailing spaces when comparing, Spark does not.

columns.name: version_count
columns.description: Number of CDC versions of the customer saved on or before @AsOfDate.

columns.name: record_updated_at
columns.description: updated_at of the version that was kept. ROW_NUMBER orders by updated_at and _row_seq ascending and keeps version_no = 1, so this is the EARLIEST version, not the current one the header describes. The migration must copy this behaviour.

columns.name: as_of_date
columns.description: The @AsOfDate parameter. It is the same on every row.

defects.title: Keeps the oldest CRM version instead of the current one
defects.description: Step 2 numbers each customer's versions with ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY updated_at, _row_seq) and keeps version_no = 1. The sort is ascending, so row 1 is the first version ever saved. Every customer with more than one version gets their original details (name, email, address, county, segment, opt-in, record_updated_at) instead of their current ones.
defects.intended_behaviour: Keep the latest version saved up to @AsOfDate, i.e. ORDER BY updated_at DESC, _row_seq DESC, as the header (CR-1702) and the step comment say.
defects.impact_query: WITH v AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM stg_customers WHERE CAST(updated_at AS DATE) <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g JOIN v ON g.customer_id = v.customer_id WHERE v.n > 1

impact.query: WITH v AS (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM stg_customers WHERE CAST(updated_at AS DATE) <= DATE'2025-12-31' GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g JOIN v ON g.customer_id = v.customer_id WHERE v.n > 1

defects.title: age_at_join counts calendar-year boundaries, not completed years
defects.description: age_at_join = DATEDIFF(YEAR, date_of_birth, customer_since) only subtracts the years. If the customer joined before their birthday that year, the age comes out one year too high.
defects.intended_behaviour: Age in completed years at the join date: subtract 1 when the month/day of customer_since is before the month/day of date_of_birth.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(g.age_at_join - (year(g.customer_since) - year(g.date_of_birth) - CASE WHEN month(g.customer_since) * 100 + day(g.customer_since) < month(g.date_of_birth) * 100 + day(g.date_of_birth) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g WHERE g.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL AND g.age_at_join <> (year(g.customer_since) - year(g.date_of_birth) - CASE WHEN month(g.customer_since) * 100 + day(g.customer_since) < month(g.date_of_birth) * 100 + day(g.date_of_birth) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(g.age_at_join - (year(g.customer_since) - year(g.date_of_birth) - CASE WHEN month(g.customer_since) * 100 + day(g.customer_since) < month(g.date_of_birth) * 100 + day(g.date_of_birth) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))), 0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g WHERE g.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL AND g.age_at_join <> (year(g.customer_since) - year(g.date_of_birth) - CASE WHEN month(g.customer_since) * 100 + day(g.customer_since) < month(g.date_of_birth) * 100 + day(g.date_of_birth) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)

defects.title: Eircode check accepts any 7-character value, including ones with a misplaced space
defects.description: eircode_valid is 'Y' whenever LEN(eircode) = 7, whatever the characters are. A 7-character value that has a space in it (really a 6-character code with a space, e.g. 'D02 X28') or contains punctuation passes. LEN also ignores trailing spaces. Only the 8-character form checks where the space is.
defects.intended_behaviour: Per the comment (3-character routing key plus 4-character unique identifier, with or without the space), valid means 7 alphanumeric characters with no space, or 3 alphanumerics, a space, then 4 alphanumerics.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g WHERE g.eircode_valid <> CASE WHEN g.eircode IS NOT NULL AND (rtrim(g.eircode) RLIKE '^[A-Za-z0-9]{7}$' OR rtrim(g.eircode) RLIKE '^[A-Za-z0-9]{3} [A-Za-z0-9]{4}$') THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g WHERE g.eircode_valid <> CASE WHEN g.eircode IS NOT NULL AND (rtrim(g.eircode) RLIKE '^[A-Za-z0-9]{7}$' OR rtrim(g.eircode) RLIKE '^[A-Za-z0-9]{3} [A-Za-z0-9]{4}$') THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END

defects.title: County spelling variants fall into region UNKNOWN
defects.description: The region CASE matches only the exact county names (for example 'Dublin'). A populated county written another way, such as 'Co. Dublin', 'County Cork', 'Tipperary North' or 'Laoighis', is mapped to 'UNKNOWN' even though it belongs to a known sales region.
defects.intended_behaviour: Normalise the county (strip 'Co.'/'County' prefixes and known variants) before mapping, so every real county gets its region and UNKNOWN is left for missing or unrecognisable values.
defects.impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g WHERE g.region = 'UNKNOWN' AND g.county IS NOT NULL AND trim(g.county) <> ''

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_dw_dim_customer g WHERE g.region = 'UNKNOWN' AND g.county IS NOT NULL AND trim(g.county) <> ''

tests.description: County values in the wrong case for every region list (DUBLIN, cork, GALWAY, donegal, LAOIS), a segment_code of 'std', and emails that differ only in case (Mary@x.ie / mary@x.ie / MARY@X.IE). Under the CI collation the legacy job puts each county in its region, flags 'std' as standard, and counts the three emails as one shared address (3). A naive Spark translation sends the counties to UNKNOWN, flags 'std' as N, and counts each email as 1. One canonical row (Dublin, STD) is included for comparison.

County values with trailing spaces for every region list ('Dublin ', 'Cork ', 'Mayo ', 'Sligo ', 'Offaly '). Emails that differ only by a trailing space ('pat@x.ie' and 'pat@x.ie '). segment_code values 'STD' (stored padded as 'STD ' in CHAR(4)) and 'PR' (padded to 'PR  '). SQL Server ignores trailing spaces, so it matches the counties to their regions, counts the shared email as 2, flags STD as Y and returns segment_code padded to 4 characters. A naive Spark translation gets UNKNOWN regions, counts 1 for each email, flags the padded 'STD ' as N, or returns an unpadded segment_code.

Builds full_name and initials with + from first_name and last_name. Both columns are NOT NULL in stg.customers, so a NULL can't be loaded and the NULL case of the trap is latent. The rows cover the edge cases that are allowed: an empty first name, an empty last name, and names with trailing spaces, which are concatenated after RTRIM. On these rows a concat() translation and the legacy job should give the same full_name and initials, and a concat_ws() translation that skips empty or NULL parts would differ only if a NULL could reach it.

Names that give 2-letter initials in T-SQL, because SUBSTRING(x,0,2) returns only the first character. A naive Spark substring(x,0,2) returns 2 characters per name, so it gives 4-letter initials. The Eircodes include trailing spaces: 'D02X285 ' and 'D02X2851  ' have a T-SQL LEN of 7 and 8, and 'D02 X285 ' has a LEN of 8 with a space at position 4. T-SQL's LEN ignores trailing spaces, so it marks some of these valid where a naive length() would not. Canonical codes ('D02X285', 'D02 X285') and an invalid code ('D02X28') are included.

Birth dates and join dates where counting year boundaries (DATEDIFF YEAR) gives a different age than counting full years elapsed. Examples: born 1990-12-31 and joined 2020-01-01 (boundaries 30, full years 29), and born 1985-06-15 and joined 2015-06-14. A row where a birthday has already passed in the join year, and a row with no date of birth (NULL age), are included as controls.

gates.reason: development run, approved by the agent (not a person's sign-off); warnings read: translator notes: 1) Collation emulation: county IN lists, segment_code = 'STD' and the email_shared_count PARTITION BY use upper(rtrim(x)). The IN-list constan
warnings:
translator notes: 1) Collation emulation: county IN lists, segment_code = 'STD' and the email_shared_count PARTITION BY use upper(rtrim(x)). The IN-list constants are the legacy literals upper-cased in Python. Stored values are output unchanged. SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS is accent-sensitive, so upper() is close enough for ASCII data. Exotic Unicode case mappings (e.g. 'ß') could differ between Spark and SQL Server in upper()/initials.
2) The lineage note says email matching is 'case- and collation-sensitive'. I treated it as case-insensitive and trailing-space-insensitive, following the TSQL-01/TSQL-02 trap findings for line 127. email_shared_count is counted over the surviving #customer rows (one per customer), not over all versions.
3) The initials use substring(x, 1, 1) on the untrimmed first_name and last_name, as in the legacy code. A leading space stays a space.
4) last_name is not RTRIMmed in the output, but first_name is (legacy behaviour, kept).
5) CHAR(n) outputs (segment_code CHAR(4), eircode_valid, is_standard_segment, marketing_opt_in CHAR(1)) are rpad'ed to n. NULL segment_code stays NULL.
6) If the source has a NULL first_name or last_name, the NOT NULL output columns (first_name, last_name, full_name, initials) would make the legacy INSERT fail. The Spark port just produces NULLs. Check that the source never has NULL names.
7) The NOLOCK read, logging, transaction and TRY/CATCH are harness concerns and were left out.
